text.content:
Long before the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} claimed her, Durga Syn was a pre-Christian nature priestess of extraordinary will, tending sacred groves and rivers in a corner of Eastern Europe untouched by encroaching Christendom. Her devotion caught the attention of Baba Yaga, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Methuselah, who offered the priestess the Embrace as an honor. Durga Syn refused, unwilling to abandon the mortal earth she served — and Baba Yaga, spurned and furious, cursed her into a withered, ancient crone as punishment, stealing her beauty and vitality in a single vindictive act. Rival @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}, eager to spite the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Methuselah and claim a prize for their own clan, tracked down the ruined priestess and Embraced her against her will, transforming Baba Yaga's curse into an eternal one.

What might have broken a lesser woman instead forged Durga Syn into one of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} clan's fiercest and most enduring enemies of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Methuselah. She warred against Baba Yaga for centuries, matching curse for curse and trick for trick across the length of Eastern Europe and Russia, a private Jyhad waged in the shadows of larger vampiric politics. Her wisdom and cunning made her a sought-after advisor; she is remembered as one of the mentors who counseled Vlad Tepes in his quest for Golconda, sharing what she knew of the Path away from the Beast. Over her long unlife she developed rituals and rites — part Ravnos deceit, part something older and stranger — that let her banish Baba Yaga's curse temporarily, restoring her stolen beauty for a time before the withering returned.

When Zapathasura's madness swept the clan in the Week of Nightmares, Durga Syn's own childer, fearing what the curse of frenzy and dissolution might do to their matriarch, staked her and hid her away for her own protection. She awoke to a changed world: Baba Yaga destroyed, the ancient curse upon her finally fading at last, and her clan scattered and diminished by Zapathasura's ruin. Durga Syn now suspects that Gehenna has truly begun, and that the Nosferatu Antediluvian itself may be stirring in the deep places of the earth. Weary from centuries of war and wary of repeating old mistakes, she has chosen to guide rather than command, quietly counseling smaller bands of Ravnos survivors — among them the loose fellowship known as the Grave Robbers — rather than seize direct leadership herself.

To history, Margaretha Geertruida Zelle — the exotic dancer and courtesan who performed under the name Mata Hari — was a spy executed by French firing squad in 1917 for allegedly passing secrets to Imperial Germany. The truth is stranger: an Indian @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}, smitten by her performances and her audacious, theatrical deceptions long before her arrest, had already taken a private interest in her. When she was condemned to die, he arranged through bribery and misdirection to recover her body swiftly after the execution, his @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} blood proving durable enough to see her through the ordeal of the firing squad and into the true death of the Embrace.

Reborn a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}, Mata Hari found her old talents for seduction, misdirection, and performance suited her new existence perfectly. She continued her work as a spy and information broker in the decades that followed, this time in service of assorted @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} figures who valued her unmatched skill at moving unnoticed through high society while extracting secrets from the powerful and the vain. Her legend as a mortal spy conveniently masks her true unlife, and those Kindred who know her real nature treat the knowledge as a closely guarded secret — for a vampire who once fooled the intelligence services of half of Europe is not an enemy, or an asset, to be spoken of carelessly.

A medieval French @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}, Marcia Felicia Licinia was an anomaly among her clan — a vampire who tried earnestly to live by chivalric virtue in an age that offered Kindred little room for such ideals. Where most @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} embraced deceit and wandering as a way of life, Marcia Felicia attempted to build a code of honor around her curse, studying the clan's history and the Path of Paradox with unusual scholarly devotion, seeking some reconciliation between her vampiric nature and the virtues she still prized.

She vanished during the Inquisition, when her haven burned to the ground under circumstances no one could ever satisfactorily explain — witch-hunters, rival Kindred, and her own clan's enemies were all suspected, and none were ever confirmed. For centuries she was presumed destroyed, a footnote in @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} history. Then, in the aftermath of the Week of Nightmares, fragments of her writings on the Path of Paradox and on the clan's deep history began resurfacing in scattered Ravnos hands, appearing in places and contexts that suggest they were deliberately, recently redistributed rather than merely rediscovered. This has fueled fervent speculation among the shattered clan that Marcia Felicia Licinia herself — or some other ancient survivor privy to her hidden writings — endures still, watching the clan's dissolution from hiding and choosing this moment, of all moments, to make her continued existence known.

To mortal eyes, Spirit Creek is an underground guitar band, perpetually touring a triangular circuit between Milwaukee, Chicago, and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}-held Detroit — a scruffy outfit playing dive bars and warehouse shows, never quite famous, never quite forgotten. In truth, the band is a kumpaniya in motion, a rolling @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} operation using the endless touring schedule as perfect cover for travel, contact, and trade that would otherwise draw unwanted attention.

The band's frontman, Doug Schoeneck, is a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} rumored by some to be one of the last surviving Deceivers, the clan's dwindling lineage of master illusionists and tricksters. Three other members round out the group, each pulling their own weight in the kumpaniya's real business: information. Spirit Creek trades secrets the way other kumpaniyas trade goods, moving intelligence between parties who would never otherwise speak to one another. Rumors persist of the band's connections to nomadic @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} packs drifting through the Midwest, to @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} archons keeping watch on the sect's borders, and even to an Inconnu Monitor who may value the band's unique vantage point on the churn of Midwestern Kindred politics. No one has confirmed which of these ties, if any, are real — which is, of course, exactly how a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} information network prefers to operate.

In East Africa, a small lineage of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} claims a heritage distinct from the Romani roots most Westerners associate with the clan: descent, however metaphorical or literal, from Anansi, the trickster spider god of West African and diasporic folklore. The eldest of this lineage — who has taken the name Anansi for their own — is rarely still long enough to be pinned to any single domain, moving constantly across the continent in a restless circuit that mirrors the wandering compulsion common to the wider clan.

Anansi's unlife is dedicated to a singular, patient project: undermining the influence European Kindred have long exerted over African domains, whether through the lingering colonial-era structures of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} or through @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} incursions following in the wake of European conquest. Anansi works through story and rumor as much as through direct action, weaving webs of information and misdirection that erode European Kindred authority one severed thread of influence at a time, in a style entirely fitting of the trickster god whose name is claimed.

Among the scattered rumors Western @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} trade about their clan's presence in Asia, none is more unsettling than the whispered tale of the Flesh-Eater — an unconfirmed report of a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} elder said to reside among the Green Courts of the Kuei-jin, the undead of the East whom Western vampires know only poorly and fear more than they understand. No Western Kindred has verified the rumor firsthand, and those few who claim to have brushed against evidence of the Flesh-Eater's existence describe it only in fragments: a name spoken in dread by Kuei-jin servants, a pattern of disappearances near a particular Green Court, an old debt owed by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} clan to powers in the East that predates any Western vampire's memory.

Whether the Flesh-Eater is a genuine ancient Ravnos who long ago crossed into Kuei-jin territory and struck some bargain for survival, a garbled misidentification of an entirely different creature, or pure invention born of Western Kindred's fear of the unknown East, remains entirely unresolved. The name persists in clan rumor precisely because no one can disprove it, and because the notion of a Ravnos elder operating inside the Kuei-jin's own courts — whether as guest, prisoner, or spy — is too tantalizing a story for the clan's storytellers to let die.

The Seven Phoenix Triad is a small jati — a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} family grouping, the clan's answer to a coterie or brood — based out of Darwin, Australia, at the continent's remote northern edge. Despite its isolated home territory, the jati is far from cut off from the wider Kindred world: it conducts the bulk of its business dealings through a network of mortal proxies operating out of Hong Kong, using the distance and the proxies' deniability to keep the jati's true membership and interests obscured from prying eyes, Kindred and mortal alike.

Little else about the Seven Phoenix Triad's specific membership, goals, or resources has spread through the wider clan's rumor mill, which is likely precisely as its members prefer it. Its choice of name — evoking both the mystical number seven and the phoenix's cycle of death and rebirth, alongside the very mortal connotation of a criminal triad — suggests a jati that understands the value of mystique and misdirection as well as any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}, using its remote base and layered proxies to conduct business at arm's length from the domains its members likely still watch closely.

Amaravati was among the clan's true ancients, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} of the Middle East who spent long ages in torpor before awakening to lead a significant portion of the clan's conversion to the true and disciplined practice of the Path of Paradox, steering @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} away from mere wanton chaos and toward the Path's deeper, more purposeful philosophy of enlightened deception. Reputed to hold close ties to the Assamites — an alliance as unusual as it was, by all accounts, genuinely productive — Amaravati's counsel and influence extended across the region's Kindred politics for centuries, lending the ancient a gravity few other @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} of any age could claim.

Amaravati vanished during the Week of Nightmares, the same catastrophe that saw Zapathasura's madness tear through the wider clan, and is presumed destroyed along with so many of the clan's other elders. No body, no haven, and no clear account of Amaravati's final night have ever surfaced, leaving the ancient's fate as uncertain as it is widely assumed — a pattern disquietingly common among the Ravnos ancients lost in that terrible week.

Rafael Schliemann operates out of a heavily guarded mansion in Rio de Janeiro, presiding over one of the most extensive and unapologetically vile enterprises any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} has built in the modern era: a global slave-trade and procurement network that treats human beings as commodities to be bought, sold, and delivered to a very select clientele. Where most @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} schemes trade in secrets, favors, or illusions, Schliemann's business is grimly literal, moving victims through channels that span continents to satisfy the appetites of Kindred and mortal patrons willing to pay extravagantly for discretion and supply.

His client list, so far as any outside party has been able to piece together, reportedly includes several @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}, whose fondness for particular vintages of blood and for arrangements that never draw official scrutiny makes them ideal, well-paying customers for exactly the kind of quiet, reliable procurement Schliemann offers. He conducts his affairs from behind the mansion's considerable defenses, insulated by wealth, hired muscle, and the simple fact that few who cross him live to complain about it — a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} who has turned the clan's gift for deception and its wanderers' reach into an engine of very profitable cruelty.

Zapathasura is the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} Antediluvian, called simply "the accursed demon" by the Eastern @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} who claim him as their creation. According to the Eastern creation myth Kuruvhnish Vrunu ("The Wounds of the Night's Sword"), a pantheon of Indian gods raised a dead man into a monster meant to destroy the asuratizayya — fallen guardian-demons who once protected mankind before turning predator upon it. Yama, Kali, Indra, Varuna, the Devi, Himavat, and Hanuman each granted the risen man a gift: vengeance, fertility, potency of blood, mastery of maya (deception), the durability of mountains, and dominion over beasts. Three gods cursed him in the same breath they empowered him: Agni and Surya doomed him to burn eventually by fire and sun, and four-headed Brahma turned away entirely, denying him natural sustenance and dooming him to eternal hunger. Brahma named him Zapathasura.

This origin story explicitly rejects any connection to Caine, a point of deep and often violent doctrinal conflict between Eastern @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} (who follow the true, older Mayaparisatya) and the Western jati descended from Roman and Egyptian lineages (who largely consider themselves Cainites like any other clan). Some Ravnos scholars, noting the story's echoes of Caine's own curses — fire, sunlight, endless hunger — wonder whether one legend is a distorted transmission of the other, carried across millennia and continents between Enoch and India. Zapathasura reputedly wrote (or is writing) an epic account of his wars against the asuratizayya, of which only fragments survive; the purported complete text, said to rest in his own hidden haven, is rumored variously to contain lost secrets of Golconda or final instructions for the Ravnos at the end of the world. Whether Zapathasura still lives, sleeps in ancient torpor beneath India, or perished amid the very demons he was created to destroy remains entirely unknown even to his own eldest childer.

Bashir is the Methuselah founder of the Bashirites, an apocalyptic Christian @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} lineage centered on Damascus, one of the oldest Western juti alongside the Alexandrites. Bashirite legend holds that Bashir personally met Christ and was charged to prepare the world for the Second Coming, a vision that has driven his childer to court chaos and strife for centuries in the belief that Christ returns only at humanity's darkest hour — a doctrine that leads Bashirites to betray Christian to Muslim, Muslim to Jew, and Jew to Christian in a self-perpetuating cycle meant to hasten Armageddon. Bashir himself Embraces only rarely, and always chooses devout Christians as childer, but he has not been seen directly by any outside chronicler; even his own get claim to know him only through visions or rare unliving visitations, leaving his true nature, location, and even continued existence deeply uncertain. His teachings have already begun to fracture: some Bashirites, like Varsik of Jerusalem, follow a warped Via Paradocis colored by Bashir's apocalyptic vision, while others follow the Road of Heaven as truer to his original intent — a doctrinal split that promises open conflict between the two factions before long.

Varsik is Bashir's childe and the eldest Bashirite that Western @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} chroniclers have been able to locate, holding court in Jerusalem near holy ground he insists on meeting near despite (or because of) the pain it causes him. Varsik is the primary source for most stories told about Bashir's founding vision, and he preaches with genuine, dangerous conviction that Christ returns only once mankind reaches its greatest possible point of strife — a belief that drives him to actively cultivate wars, betrayals, and religious atrocities across the Holy Land, treating the Crusades themselves as fuel for his apocalyptic project.

Of particular note among Varsik's childer is Etienne de Fauberge, a knight of the First Crusade Embraced at Antioch in 1099 for the virtue he showed when his fellow crusaders turned to slaughter and looting. Varsik hoped Etienne's piety would let him enter Acre, the city reputed to hold the True Cross and barred to Cainites by its holy influence; even @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} blood proved unable to overcome that ward, though Etienne's obsessive, repeated attempts to walk into the flame-wracked city eventually convinced Varsik to grant him the surrounding domain instead. Varsik maintains numerous havens throughout Jerusalem for Bashirite use and keeps close correspondence with Etienne, growing visibly concerned in his letters that his childe's role as an information broker to Cainites of every clan — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} reportedly among them — has eroded Etienne's devotion to the coming Armageddon.

Etienne de Fauberge was a knight of the First Crusade, Embraced by the Bashirite elder Varsik at Antioch in 1099 after standing back in horror while his fellow crusaders raped and pillaged the captured city. Varsik hoped Etienne's genuine piety might let him walk into Acre — the city reputed to hold the True Cross, and warded against Cainites by its holy influence — but even @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} blood could not carry him past that barrier, though Etienne returned again and again, taking the flames that scorched his flesh each time as a kind of holy atonement for his vampiric nature.

Unable to enter the city he became obsessed with, Etienne instead claimed the domain surrounding Acre as his own fief at Varsik's urging, forestalling any other Cainite from doing so. Over the following years, power and long practice have eroded much of his original faith: he now walks openly among Acre's merchants and residents, feeling the holy pain constantly, and has become less a holy defender than an information broker, offering sanctuary to Cainites of any clan — even, reportedly, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} — in exchange for information or services. His domain's one hard rule is that no violence may occur within a mile of Acre's walls; his mortal servants drag offenders bodily into the city itself, where the holy influence deals with them permanently. Varsik has written to Etienne expressing growing concern that his childe has strayed from his sacred purpose into worldly commerce with pagans and heathens alike.

Ramessu is the eldest of the Alexandrites that Western chroniclers can identify, ruling from Alexandria with an antiquated, formal etiquette that harkens back to Egypt's pharaonic courts. He refuses to name his own sire, instead laying claim to a lineage of pharaohs and gods, and holds court from a throne room said to rival any pharaonic hall, draped in cloth of gold and covered in enameled jewelry, its walls inscribed with picture-writing whose glyphs subtly move when watched long enough to suggest whole stories unfolding. Ramessu does not command the Alexandrites outright, but his advice carries the weight of command among them regardless, and the lineage's elders in particular maintain his antiquated affectations of dress and protocol even as its ancillae and neonates drift toward more contemporary vagabond airs.

The Alexandrites under Ramessu's influence hold the distinction of being one of the two oldest @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} juti in the Western world (alongside the Phaedymites), and the largest, with members ranging across Africa, the Levant, and Europe. They are notably cold toward the recent wave of Eastern @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} migrants, resenting most sharply the newcomers' claim that the Roma people share Egyptian origins — a claim the Alexandrites regard as poaching on herds and lineages they have cultivated for centuries, and one that has already sparked open feuds between the two populations.

Karmenita Yoryari is the founder of the Yoryari, a jati that splintered off from the hedonistic, decadent Sybarites when Karmenita chose to part ways with her own sire — the very founder of the Sybarite lineage and its debauched, Rome-born interpretation of the Via Paradocis. Rather than pursue excess for its own sake, Karmenita built a more spiritual, purposeful reading of Paradox around Lisbon, teaching that adherents must act with reason: power structures and stagnant institutions must be worn down and destroyed, not out of pleasure, but to make way for something new before calcification sets in entirely. Taken to its logical extreme, this could mean unmaking Cainite society itself, an ambition Karmenita's more zealous followers occasionally pursue through Furore bands and similarly destructive projects.

Karmenita maintains a lavish estate near Lisbon and never speaks of her Sybarite sire except in the most hateful terms, suggesting a bitter falling out whose full details she has never shared even with her own childer. Her eldest childe, Iago Castille, practices piracy across the Mediterranean, Iberia, France, and Britain as far north as the North Sea, while many other Yoryari travel as pilgrims or merchants among mortals, using that guise to keep watch over the Iberian Cainite courts as Karmenita's eyes and ears without drawing the scrutiny more established clans might otherwise bring to bear on a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} jati.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Ravnos, Chapter Three; Libellus Sanguinis IV: Thieves in the Night, Book One: Charlatans
